Figure 1: An observation from our text-based web-browsing environment, as shown to human demonstrators (left) and models (right). The web page text has been abridged for illustrative purposes.

Figure2: Human evaluations on ELI5 comparing against (a) demonstrations collected using our web browser, (b) the highest-voted answer for each question. The amount of rejection sampling (the n in best-of-n) was chosen to be compute-efficient (see Figure8). Error bars represent ±1 standard error.

Figure 4: Preference of RL models over BC models, with (right) and without (left) using rejection sampling. RL slightly improves preference, but only when not using rejection sampling. Error bars represent ±1 standard error.
Figure6: BC scaling, varying the proportion of the demonstration dataset and parameter count of the policy.
Figure8: Best-of-n scaling, varying the parameter count of the policy and reward model together, as well as the number of answers sampled.
